feedback.problem: What is the center and radius of the circle with equation $(x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}=9?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The general equation of a circle with radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ is 

$$
(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}={r}^{2}.
$$

Let's compare the general equation to our equation side-by-side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2} & ={r}^{2} \\ (x-2)^{2}+(y+2)^{2} & =9 \\ (x-2)^{2}+(y-(-2))^{2} & ={3}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We see that $a=2,$ $b=-2,$ and $r=3.$ 

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(2,-2)$ and its radius is $3.$
